subtitulo: Feedback on someone's cooking — behaviour, not character
descripcion: Feedback in English professional culture follows conventions strong enough to learn as formulas. The core one: describe behaviour and impact, not character. *You were unprepared* is character; *the deck arrived an hour before the meeting, so we spent fifteen minutes reading* is behaviour and impact — and only the second gives the person something to change.

filas: Can I give you some feedback on the report?
When the estimate changed without a note…
What's your read on why it slipped?
I might be missing context here.

ejemplos.texto: *Can I give you some feedback on the report? Two things worked, one didn't.*
*When the estimate changed without a note, the client assumed we'd hidden it. That's the bit I'd do differently.*
*I might be missing context — what's your read on why it slipped?*
*What's your read on why it slipped?*

notas: Asking permission first is near-mandatory in most English-speaking workplaces.
The praise-criticism-praise sandwich is now widely disliked: people hear only the praise, or wait for the middle.
Naming your own uncertainty makes the feedback easier to accept without weakening it.

es.en: Spanish has the pieces of structured feedback («lo que funciona muy bien es…» – what works really well is…; «lo que yo cambiaría es…» – what I'd change is…), so the four slots can be filled with direct equivalents.
es.es: El español tiene las piezas del feedback estructurado («lo que funciona muy bien es…» – «what works really well is…»; «lo que yo cambiaría es…» – «what I'd change is…»), por lo que las cuatro casillas pueden llenarse con equivalentes directos.

de.en: «Was gut funktioniert, ist…» and «was ich ändern würde, ist…» correspond directly to the English slots, including the cleft structure. Structured feedback therefore transfers directly.
de.de: «Was gut funktioniert, ist…» und «was ich ändern würde, ist…» entsprechen direkt den englischen Mustern, einschließlich der Spaltsatzstruktur. Strukturiertes Feedback lässt sich daher direkt übertragen.

it.en: «Quello che funziona bene è…» and «cambierei…» correspond directly to the English slots. Structured feedback therefore transfers directly.
it.it: «Quello che funziona bene è…» e «cambierei…» corrispondono direttamente agli schemi inglesi. Il feedback strutturato si trasferisce quindi direttamente.

fr.en: «Ce qui marche bien, c'est…» and «ce que je changerais, c'est…» correspond directly to the English slots, including the cleft structure. Structured feedback therefore transfers directly.
fr.fr: «Ce qui marche bien, c'est…» et «ce que je changerais, c'est…» correspondent directement aux cadres anglais, y compris la structure clivée. Le feedback structuré se transfère donc directement.

pt.en: «O que funciona bem é…» and «o que eu mudaria é…» correspond directly to the English slots. Structured feedback therefore transfers directly.
pt.pt: «O que funciona bem é…» e «o que eu mudaria é…» correspondem diretamente aos moldes ingleses. O feedback estruturado se transfere diretamente.

errores: *You always* / *You never* — indefensible, and guarantees defensiveness.
Softening until the message is invisible. If they leave unsure there was a problem, there wasn't one.
Feedback on personality rather than output.

es: «*No es por criticar, pero*» rendered as *It's not for criticising, but* instead of *I don't mean to criticise, but*.
de: «*Das passt schon*» rendered as *That fits already*, which sounds odd and too faint, instead of *That works* or *That's fine*.
it: «*Non per criticare, ma*» rendered as *Not for criticising, but* instead of *I don't mean to criticise, but*.
fr: «*Sans vouloir te vexer*» rendered as *Without wanting to vex you* instead of *No offence, but*.
pt: «*Não é por nada, mas*» rendered as *It's not for nothing, but* instead of *No offence, but*.

redemittel.expresion: How do you want to handle it?

mision.consigna: A friend asked for honest feedback on a dinner they cooked for you. Give it.
requisitos: describe behaviour and effect, not character

microtareas.texto: Write two feedback sentences about a meal: one about the cook, one about what happened on the plate. Keep the second.
Rewrite *You always overdo the salt* as behaviour + impact.
Record 90 seconds giving feedback on a *balanced diet* someone is trying. End with *How do you want to handle it?*

autochequeo: Is every point behaviour, or did a character judgement slip in?
Is the impact stated, or only implied?
Would the person leave knowing exactly what to change?
Did I ask permission and hand the turn back?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the feedback. (1) Mark each point as behaviour or character. (2) Is the impact stated or only implied? (3) Would the person know exactly what to change? (4) Flag where I softened it into invisibility. Do not rewrite the text.
